questions.question: The man ______ is standing at the gate is my English teacher.
questions.explanation: The antecedent 'the man' refers to a person and acts as the subject in the clause, so 'who' is correct.

questions.question: I will never forget the day ______ I first met you.
questions.explanation: The antecedent 'the day' refers to time, so the adverb 'when' is used.

questions.question: Could you tell me ______ you will go to Beijing?
questions.explanation: The clause needs a time adverbial; 'when' fits the context of asking about time.

questions.question: I don't know ______ he will come tomorrow.
questions.explanation: The sentence expresses uncertainty about whether he will come, so 'if' is correct.

questions.question: ______ it rains heavily, we will stay at home.
questions.explanation: This is a conditional adverbial clause; 'If' introduces the condition.

questions.question: She was late ______ she got up too late this morning.
questions.explanation: The second clause explains the reason for the first clause, so 'because' is correct.

questions.question: He decided ______ a new bicycle for his birthday.
questions.explanation: The verb 'decide' is followed by an infinitive: 'decide to do something'.

questions.question: ______ is good for our health.
questions.explanation: A gerund is needed as the subject of the sentence; 'Swimming' acts as a noun.

questions.question: Tom got up late this morning. He ran to school ______ stopping.
questions.explanation: The context implies Tom did not stop; 'without' is correct.

questions.question: (Passage: Lucy loves reading. She visits the library every Saturday...) Q: How often does Lucy visit the library?
questions.explanation: The passage clearly states 'every Saturday'.

questions.question: Which relative pronouns can be used to refer to people? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: 'Who', 'whom', and 'that' can refer to people; 'which' refers to things.

questions.question: Which words can introduce an object clause? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: 'That', 'what', and 'if' can introduce object clauses; 'because' introduces reason clauses.

questions.question: Which conjunctions can introduce a conditional clause? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: 'If', 'unless', and 'as long as' introduce conditions; 'because' introduces reasons.

questions.question: Which forms are correct after 'enjoy'? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: 'Enjoy' is followed by a gerund: 'enjoy doing something'.

questions.question: This is the house ______ I lived ten years ago.
questions.explanation: The antecedent 'the house' refers to a place, so 'where' is used.

questions.question: Do you know ______ he is waiting for?
questions.explanation: The object clause asks about a person as the object of 'waiting for'.

questions.question: ______ you study hard, you will pass the exam.
questions.explanation: This is a conditional clause; 'If' introduces the condition.

questions.question: My mother asked me ______ (finish) my homework first.
questions.explanation: 'Ask somebody to do something' requires the infinitive.

questions.question: The old man walked ______ (slow) down the street.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the verb 'walked'.

questions.question: In the sentence 'The book which I bought is interesting', 'which' refers to the book.
questions.explanation: 'Which' is a relative pronoun referring to the antecedent 'the book'.

questions.question: Object clauses must always use the conjunction 'that'.
questions.explanation: Object clauses can also use 'if', 'whether', 'what', etc.

questions.question: 'Stop to do' means stopping one action in order to do another.
questions.explanation: 'Stop to do' means stopping in order to start another action; 'stop doing' means ceasing an action.

questions.question: (Passage: Tom is a helpful boy. He often helps his classmates with their lessons...) Q: What kind of boy is Tom? Give one example from the passage.
questions.answer: Tom is a helpful boy. He often helps his classmates with their lessons.
questions.explanation: The passage describes Tom as helpful and gives this example.

questions.question: The school ______ we visited last week was built in 1950.
questions.explanation: The antecedent 'the school' is the object of 'visited' in the clause, so 'that' is used.

questions.question: This is the best film ______ I have ever seen.
questions.explanation: When the antecedent is modified by a superlative, 'that' is preferred over 'which'.

questions.question: I wonder ______ they will arrive on time.
questions.explanation: The verb 'wonder' expresses uncertainty, so 'if' or 'whether' is appropriate.

questions.question: He told me ______ he had finished his work.
questions.explanation: The clause is a statement; 'that' introduces the object clause.

questions.question: ______ he is young, he knows a lot about science.
questions.explanation: The contrast between being young and knowing a lot indicates a concession; 'Although' is correct.

questions.question: We will start the meeting ______ everyone arrives.
questions.explanation: 'As soon as' indicates that one event happens immediately after another.

questions.question: The boy ______ (stand) there is my brother.
questions.explanation: The present participle 'standing' acts as an attribute modifying 'the boy'.

questions.question: I heard someone ______ my name in the corridor.
questions.explanation: 'Hear somebody doing something' means perceiving an action in progress.

questions.question: The weather was terrible, ______ we decided to stay indoors.
questions.explanation: The bad weather caused the decision to stay indoors; 'so' shows result.

questions.question: (Passage: The Internet has changed our lives greatly. It helps us get information quickly...) Q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: B. The Internet has changed our lives.
C. People should not use the Internet.
questions.explanation: The first sentence states the main idea: the Internet has changed our lives.

questions.question: In which situations can 'that' be used instead of 'which'? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: 'That' is used after superlatives, indefinite pronouns, and 'all'; not after a comma in non-restrictive clauses.

questions.question: Which of the following can be used as the object of 'know'? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Noun clauses can act as objects; 'because he left' is an adverbial clause.

questions.question: Which conjunctions show contrast? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: 'Although', 'while', and 'however' show contrast; 'because' shows reason.

questions.question: Which sentences use gerunds correctly? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: 'Want' is followed by an infinitive, not a gerund.

questions.question: The reason ______ he was absent is still unknown.
questions.explanation: The antecedent 'the reason' requires the relative adverb 'why'.

questions.question: Can you tell me ______ the train leaves?
questions.explanation: The clause asks about time; 'when' is the correct conjunction.

questions.question: Work hard ______ you will succeed.
questions.explanation: This is a coordinate structure: 'Work hard and you will succeed'.

questions.question: The book is worth ______ (read).
questions.explanation: 'Be worth doing' is a fixed expression requiring a gerund.

questions.question: She put on her coat and ______ (leave) the room quietly.
questions.explanation: The past tense is needed to match 'put on'.

questions.question: In non-restrictive relative clauses, we can use 'that' instead of 'which'.
questions.explanation: Non-restrictive clauses use 'which', not 'that'.

questions.question: 'Unless' means the same as 'if not'.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' is equivalent to 'if ... not'.

questions.question: 'Remember doing' means remembering something you did in the past.
questions.explanation: 'Remember doing' means recalling a past action; 'remember to do' means not forgetting to do something.

questions.question: (Passage about exam stress) Q: What are two ways to reduce exam stress mentioned in the passage?
questions.explanation: The passage mentions these two suggestions from experts.

questions.question: Change the direct speech into an object clause: 'Is he coming tomorrow?' She asked me.
questions.answer: She asked me if/whether he was coming the next day.
questions.explanation: Indirect questions use 'if/whether' and backshift the tense.

questions.question: He is the only one of the students who ______ passed the exam.
questions.explanation: The antecedent is 'the only one', a singular noun, so the verb agrees with the singular.

questions.question: The meeting ______ we are looking forward to will be held next week.
questions.explanation: 'The meeting' is the object of 'look forward to', so a relative pronoun is needed.

questions.question: It is uncertain ______ he will be able to come.
questions.explanation: 'Uncertain' implies doubt, so 'whether' is the correct conjunction.

questions.question: ______ he said at the meeting surprised everybody.
questions.explanation: The subject clause needs a pronoun that acts as the object of 'said'; 'What' is correct.

questions.question: ______ had I arrived home when it began to rain.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly...when', 'No sooner...than', and 'Scarcely...when' all express immediate succession.

questions.question: ______ you may do, you must do it well.
questions.explanation: 'Whatever' acts as the object of 'do', meaning 'no matter what'.

questions.question: ______ (give) more time, I could have done better.
questions.explanation: The past participle 'Given' introduces a conditional participle clause.

questions.question: The problem ______ (discuss) at the meeting now is very important.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'at the meeting now' indicates the action is in progress, so the present participle passive is used.

questions.question: The old house, ______ (abandon) for years, finally collapsed in the storm.
questions.explanation: The past participle 'abandoned' indicates a passive and completed action.

questions.question: (Passage about exercise benefits) Q: What is an additional benefit of exercise besides physical health?
questions.explanation: The passage states exercise boosts memory and concentration.

questions.question: Which sentences contain non-restrictive relative clauses? (Select all that apply)
options: A. Tom, who is my friend, is kind.
B. The book which is red is mine.
C. The man, whom I met, is kind.
D. All books that I have are good.
questions.explanation: Non-restrictive clauses are set off by commas and provide extra information.

questions.question: Which of the following are correct subject clauses? (Select all that apply)
options: A. What he said is true.
B. That he will come is certain.
C. Whether he comes doesn't matter.
D. If he comes is not known.
questions.explanation: Subject clauses cannot be introduced by 'if'; use 'whether' instead.

questions.question: Which sentences use inversion correctly? (Select all that apply)
options: A. Hardly had I left when it rained.
B. No sooner had he left than it rained.
C. Not only does he swim but also runs.
D. Although he is young, he works hard.
questions.explanation: 'Although' does not trigger inversion; the others are correct inverted structures.

questions.question: Which structures use the perfect participle? (Select all that apply)
options: A. Having finished work, he went home.
B. The work finished, he went home.
C. Having been told the news, she cried.
D. Being tired, he stopped working.
questions.explanation: The perfect participle indicates an action completed before the main verb.

questions.question: I have two brothers, both of ______ are doctors.
questions.explanation: 'Both of whom' is the correct preposition + relative pronoun structure in non-restrictive clauses.

questions.question: The question is ______ we can finish the task on time.
questions.explanation: The predicative clause expresses uncertainty; 'whether' is correct.

questions.question: ______ (work) hard, you will make progress.
questions.explanation: The present participle introduces a conditional clause.

questions.question: The book is said ______ (translate) into many languages.
questions.explanation: 'Be said to' plus the perfect infinitive passive indicates a completed passive action.

questions.question: ______ (judge) from his accent, he must be from the south.
questions.explanation: 'Judging from' is a fixed expression used as an independent comment.

questions.question: In 'The man who I spoke to is my uncle', 'who' can be replaced by 'whom'.
questions.explanation: When the relative pronoun is the object of a preposition, 'whom' is formally correct, though 'who' is often used informally.

questions.question: 'Were I you, I would accept the offer' is a correct inverted conditional sentence.
questions.explanation: This is an inverted form of 'If I were you', omitting 'if' and inverting the subject and verb.

questions.question: 'Having been warned' indicates a passive action that happened before the main verb.
questions.explanation: The perfect passive participle shows a prior passive action.

questions.question: (Passage about plastic pollution) Q: What are two measures to tackle plastic pollution mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: Developing new materials that break down naturally and introducing laws to limit single-use plastics.
questions.explanation: The passage mentions both scientific development and government legislation.
